scope_label: costs attributable to defects and other quality failures
definition: Cost of poor quality (COPQ) is the estimated cost attributable to failures to meet relevant quality requirements.
explanation: It can include scrap and rework found before delivery, and returns, warranty work, complaints, or other consequences found afterward. Some costs are difficult to observe or assign.

An estimate needs a stated accounting boundary, time period, and basis for attributing costs. Prevention and appraisal costs are often reported separately as costs of achieving quality; naming the convention avoids misleading comparisons.
